title: Mark-up and margin on four shoe lines
objective: Calculate mark-up (profit / cost) and margin (profit / price), and test the margin against a target with IF.
instructions: Profit is price less cost. In D2:D5, work out the mark-up: profit divided by cost. In E2:E5, work out the margin: profit divided by price. Answers are decimals (0.07 means 7%). In F2:F5, show On target when the margin is at or above the target margin in G2, otherwise show Below target. Refer to G2 with $G$2 instead of typing the target.
hints: Profit is price minus cost, so use brackets: =(C2-B2)/B2 for mark-up. The only thing that changes for margin is the number you divide by.
Margin divides the profit by the selling price: =(C2-B2)/C2.
For the check, compare the margin with the target: =IF(E2>=$G$2,"On target","Below target"). >= means at or above.
